newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to nominate Clark as NATO commander.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to nominate Clark as NATO commander.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has chosen U.S. Army Gen. Wesley Clark to become commander of all allied NATO forces in Europe and head of U.S. forces in Europe, a senior Pentagon official said on Monday.

Clark, 52, speaks Russian and was a key member of the American team that helped broker the 1995 Dayton peace accords on Bosnia. He is currently based in Panama as commander of U.S. forces in Latin America and would replace retiring U.S. Army Gen. George Joulwan in the NATO job at Mons, Belgium.

The Pentagon official, who asked not to be identified, confirmed a Washington Post report that announcement of the nomination, which would require approval from other Atlantic alliance countries, could come as early as Monday.

"The job of SACEUR (Supreme Allied Commander of NATO forces Europe) and of comander of U.S. troops in Europe requires somebody to be both a soldier and a statesman, to deal not only with military officials but the leaders of governments and Russia," the official said.
"Clark fills the bill," said the official, adding that Defense Secretary William Cohen had recommended the general to Clinton after interviewing more than a dozen potential candidates.

The job of SACEUR has been held by U.S. military officers since the end of the second World War and Clark, a West Point military academy graduate and former Rhodes scholar who attended England's Oxford University, is expected to be approved by the allies, according to the Pentagon official.
